# Independent outer-observer generated review

The first held source (`b2fa9a4b…`) ran 18 generated test methods. Seventeen methods had no failures; one method produced three failing subcases. The observer accepted contradictory timeout/launch/output-limit flags when the same fake helper result claimed successful completion. The current pinned real helper derives completion as false for those flags, so this is an independent consistency-check gap rather than an observed actual-helper failure. See [initial finding](initial-review.json) and [unaltered first execution](first/execution.json).

The generated fixtures execute the observer in isolated temporary directories with an inert, captured support module. Real subprocess targets, Git, repository guards and network are forbidden by test patches. All inputs and results are invented. No archive, private custody, actual production helper or upstream validator is invoked. The fixed routes, five tool pins, source drift, one-shot reservation, canonical output matching, regular-file boundaries and partial-publication paths are covered.

Post-child state checks occur before log writes, including when those writes fail. Late packet-publication and outer stdout failures cannot return success, but a packet can already exist. Its existence is therefore insufficient: root must independently observe the outer wrapper's actual successful process exit. The dependent recorder's separate validation already requires the three failure flags to be literal false; that source-only observation does not turn this failing observer run into a pass.

Final disposition and any amended-source invocation remain pending. This is software-observation evidence only, with no scientific admission or actual source operation.
